questions.question: position: relative offsets an element:

options.text: From its NORMAL position, leaving its original space occupied

questions.explanation: relative shifts visually via top/left/right/bottom but keeps its spot in flow (also establishes a positioning context for absolutes).

questions.question: position: absolute takes an element:

options.text: Out of normal flow, positioned relative to nearest positioned ancestor

questions.explanation: absolute removes the element from flow; it anchors to the nearest ancestor with position != static, else the initial containing block.

questions.question: position: fixed anchors to:

options.text: The viewport (stays put on scroll), unless an ancestor has a transform

questions.explanation: fixed positions relative to the viewport; an ancestor with transform/filter creates a containing block, breaking the viewport anchor.

questions.question: position: sticky behaves like:

options.text: relative until it crosses a threshold, then sticks like fixed within its parent

questions.explanation: sticky toggles between relative and fixed based on scroll position, constrained to its containing parent — great for headers.

questions.question: z-index only affects elements with:

options.text: A positioning value other than static (or flex/grid items)

questions.explanation: z-index applies to positioned elements (relative/absolute/fixed/sticky) and flex/grid items; static elements ignore it.

questions.question: z-index stacking context is created by, among others:

options.text: position + z-index, opacity < 1, transform, will-change, filter

questions.explanation: Many properties create a new stacking context, trapping child z-index within it — a common 'why won't it overlap' gotcha.

questions.question: To center with absolute positioning you can use:
questions.explanation: The translate(-50%,-50%) trick offsets by the element's own size to truly center it within the positioned ancestor.

questions.question: A common use of position: relative is:

options.text: Creating a positioning context for absolutely-positioned children (tooltips, badges)

questions.explanation: Setting a wrapper to relative lets child absolutes anchor to it instead of the viewport — essential for overlays/badges.
